articles_hidden.title: Intersectorialidad y su rol frente a la inequidad en salud en Bogotá, Colombia: una revisión rápida de la literatura
articles_hidden.authors: Alejandra Rivera Rodríguez; Catalina Penagos Torijano; Daniel Alejandro Ramírez Triana; Iván Felipe Padilla Cabrera; Francisco Palencia-Sánchez
articles_hidden.abstract:
Introducción: La intersectorialidad en salud permite coordinar diferentes sectores —político, social y económico, entre otros— para actuar sobre los determinantes de la salud y las inequidades sanitarias. En Colombia, los cambios históricos de carácter sociopolítico y económico han contribuido a profundizar las desigualdades en diversos territorios y, por ende, han generado dificultades de acceso al sistema de salud, fragilidad institucional y menor cohesión social.
Objetivo: Se realizó una revisión rápida de la literatura para identificar y sintetizar la evidencia disponible sobre la intersectorialidad en salud y su relación con las inequidades en el sistema de salud colombiano, así como para determinar la aplicabilidad de las estrategias identificadas al contexto de Bogotá.
Método: Se desarrolló una revisión rápida de la literatura mediante búsquedas en Scopus, Embase, ProQuest, SciELO, BIREME y fuentes de literatura gris. Se utilizaron términos MeSH y DeCS, y se siguieron las recomendaciones de PRISMA 2020. Las referencias recuperadas se exportaron a Rayyan para su organización, eliminación de duplicados y selección. Posteriormente, dos revisores independientes y cegados realizaron el cribado por título y resumen y, luego, la evaluación de los textos completos, con el fin de reducir el sesgo de selección.
Resultados: Se identificaron 324 registros. Tras aplicar los filtros definidos en las bases de datos, se excluyeron 276 y, después de eliminar un duplicado, quedaron 47 registros para el cribado por título y resumen. De estos, 20 pasaron a evaluación en texto completo y 5 cumplieron los criterios de inclusión. Además, se incorporó una fuente de literatura gris, para un total de 6 documentos en la síntesis final. Los hallazgos indican que la intersectorialidad puede contribuir al abordaje de las inequidades en salud, aunque su implementación depende de diversos facilitadores y barreras. La evidencia disponible sobre su impacto es limitada y heterogénea.
Conclusión: La evidencia sobre la intersectorialidad en salud en Bogotá es limitada, exploratoria y predominantemente cualitativa. Permite describir patrones y experiencias vinculadas a contextos específicos, pero en su mayoría no evalúa los efectos de las estrategias. No obstante, se identificaron factores consistentes entre los estudios: la voluntad política, la planeación conjunta y la participación comunitaria fueron facilitadores recurrentes, mientras que la fragmentación institucional y la discontinuidad de los procesos constituyeron las principales barreras. Dado que ninguno de los estudios incluidos realizó seguimiento posterior al periodo evaluado, la sostenibilidad institucional de las estrategias intersectoriales continúa siendo un reto por resolver.

articles_hidden.title: Service Colonisation of the Public Health Model of Bereavement Support: A Critical Review and a Refined Model
articles_hidden.authors: Yong Hao Ng; Bruce Rumbold; Torsten Schwalbach; Samar Aoun
articles_hidden.abstract: The public health model of bereavement support, introduced in 2012, proposed a tiered framework that emphasised community networks’ contributions, informal resources, and shared responsibility across sectors in addition to professional clinical intervention. This study systematically examines how the model has been taken up in the research literature through a combined deductive content analysis and Foucauldian-informed discourse analysis of 252 peer-reviewed articles that cite the model’s foundational papers. The deductive analysis reveals that individually oriented and clinically focused components, particularly triage, epidemiology, and risk factors, dominate the corpus, while community resources and resource allocation remain peripheral. The discourse analysis identifies three interconnected discursive formations: an over-psychologisation that evaluates bereavement as psychiatric risk; an over-professionalisation that positions health professionals as central authorities and renders communities subordinate; and a governmental logic that treats risks, needs, and support as fixed, individually centred categories. Together, these formations constitute what we term service colonisation, in which the institutional norms of the health sciences reshape a broad social framework into a tool for organising clinical resource distribution. This narrowing has material consequences for which services are funded, which populations are recognised as needing support, and whose knowledge is privileged in the design of responses. We propose a refined model that reframes need beyond clinical risk, repositions communities as constitutive agents rather than passive resources, introduces dynamism into the tiered structures, and foregrounds social and structural determinants of bereavement. These findings have implications for how bereavement support is conceptualised, researched, and organised across health and social care systems.

articles_hidden.title: Drivers of household electricity demand in highly electrified markets
articles_hidden.authors: Reza Serati; Anna Kristina Zinn; Siamak Layeghy; Bettina Grün; Marius Portmann; Sara Dolnicar
articles_hidden.abstract: As the world transitions to renewable energies, the structure of national electricity markets will change. Queensland (Australia) is a pioneer market; it is one of the most highly electrified markets internationally. This study analyses drivers of household grid electricity imports using operational smart-meter data from 1,119,389 households and two linked surveys. Solar and battery ownership, dwelling type, household size, pool and electric-vehicle ownership, and climate zone are key drivers. Having a solar system, living in a unit and in smaller households is associated with lower electricity imports. Larger households with a pool and electric vehicles import more electricity. We discuss these findings in the context of previous studies of drivers of household electricity use conducted in more traditional power markets. By distinguishing grid imports from total household consumption, we show how distributed generation and storage reshape network demand and provide new evidence for forecasting and planning in highly electrified markets.

articles_hidden.title: Benefit conditionality, sanction rules and the self-rated health of the unemployed: a longitudinal analysis of European countries
articles_hidden.authors: Christoph Henking; Aaron Reeves
articles_hidden.abstract:
Background
The health effects of unemployment vary across European countries. This study examines whether cross-country differences in behavioural conditionality - such as job-search requirements, availability requirements and statutory strictness of sanctions rules - may shape these health effects, and which aspects of conditionality matter most.
Methods
We combined panel data from the European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC, 2014–2019) with OECD indicators on activation policy strictness in 30 countries. Using first-difference regression models, we estimated the effect of becoming unemployed on changes in self-rated health (five-point scale) and tested whether this effect was moderated by the strictness of each policy dimension. We controlled for individual-level and macroeconomic variables.
Results
Becoming unemployed was linked to a small but significant decline in self-rated health (−0.05, 95% CI[−0.06, −0.04]). This decline was steeper in countries with stricter statutory sanction rules (interaction = −0.04 [−0.08, −0.004]), ranging from −0.053 [−0.098, −0.017] in low-sanction countries to −0.105 [−0.135, −0.078] in high-sanction countries. Job-search and availability requirements showed no significant moderation.
Interpretation
Stricter statutory sanction rules are associated with worse self-rated health among job seekers. Reducing reliance on sanctions and ensuring supportive activation systems could help protect health during unemployment.

articles_hidden.title: Mapping disability inclusion in Canadian park employment: A scoping review of academic and organizational evidence
articles_hidden.authors: Hannah Dudney; Zeyad Ghulam; Tilak Dutta
articles_hidden.abstract:
Objective: The objective of this scoping review is to map how disability inclusion and accessibility are considered in Canadian park employment literature and organizational discourse. The review will identify and summarize both peer-reviewed literature and organizational evidence to examine how workplace accessibility and disability inclusion are addressed in these settings, and the extent to which they are absent. 

Introduction: Parks and protected areas in Canada are key public-facing service environments that increasingly emphasize accessibility and inclusion in relation to visitor experiences. However, less is known about how these organizations approach employment inclusion for people with disabilities, across both academic literature and organizational documents.  

Inclusion criteria: This review will include sources that concern employment-related stakeholders such as employers, employees, managers or other decision-makers (Population). Literature, policies, and other organizational discourse will be examined to determine the extent they consider disability, accessibility, and disability-inclusive employment (Concept). The search will be limited to Canadian parks and protected area organizations, with a focus on national, provincial, and territorial parks (Context). Sources will not be required to focus on disability and accessibility, provided they contain employment-related content. Both peer-reviewed literature and grey literature will be searched and reviewed. 

Methods: Peer-reviewed literature will include a search of the following collections: EBSCO (EconLit, Business Source Premier), ProQuest (ASSIA, PAIS Index, Policy File Index, Worldwide Political Science Abstracts, IBSS), and Web of Science (Core Collection: SSCI, SCI-Expanded, ESCI, AHCI, CPCI-SSH, CPCI-S, BKCI-SSH). Grey literature will be systematically searched through official websites of Canadian national, provincial and territorial park agencies in Canada, with targeted searches for employment and human resource policies and reports. Searches will not be restricted by date but will be limited to English-language sources. 

The targeted search will take place in September 2026. All identified sources will be imported into Covidence and screened in two stages (title/abstract and full text) against the inclusion criteria. Data will be extracted to capture document characteristics and accessibility or disability inclusion-related content. Findings will be reported using frequency counts and narrative descriptions to map key concepts, evidence types, and gaps. Any deviations from standard JBI scoping review methodology will be documented and justified.

articles_hidden.title: Searching for Serendipity
articles_hidden.authors: Isaac Tucker; Martin Gonzalez-Cabello; Olav Sorenson
articles_hidden.abstract: Serendipity would seem to preclude purposeful search. To understand the relationship between search behavior and the probability of a serendipitous discovery, we propose a formal modeling framework based on the 𝑁𝐾model. Our simulations suggest that searchers with a clear hypothesis convert good fortune into fitness or value far more effectively. Searchers that pursue their theories through incremental steps instead of long-distance jumps have the highest rates of serendipitous success. Our model also provides insight into the role of bias, inaccurate or incorrect beliefs, and the ruggedness of the terrain in determining the rate of serendipitous discovery. Our results demonstrate the distinct roles of intent and information in finding novel, valuable discoveries.

articles_hidden.title: Rethinking Revictimization
articles_hidden.authors: Joyce Mok
articles_hidden.abstract: Survivors of childhood abuse have a heightened risk of experiencing adulthood interpersonal violence. Existing theories explain revictimization through the victim’s deficits and past experiences of violence. These theories fail to explain the causes of revictimization, can lead to ineffective interventions, and can harm victims. This article presents a secondary analysis of the qualitative literature inspired by Eve Tuck’s formulation of desire-based research, which originally aimed to address similar narratives in the fields of education research and Indigenous studies. This analysis shows the benefits of a theoretical approach that situates the individual’s motivations within an interpersonal, social, and cultural context.

articles_hidden.title: Representation Without Power: Far Right Electoral Success and Violence in Weimar Germany
articles_hidden.authors: Felix Haass; Alexander De Juan; Daniel Bischof; Henry Thomson
articles_hidden.abstract: Far right parties often win elections without gaining access to power. Do such outcomes pacify extremist movements, or can they fuel violence? We study this question in Weimar Germany after the July 1932 Reichstag election, when the Nazi Party became the largest parliamentary force but remained outside government. We digitize Nazi candidate lists and Prussian police records on street violence, linking riots to candidates' home towns. Using a regression discontinuity design around district list cutoffs, we compare towns whose Nazi candidates narrowly entered parliament with towns whose candidates narrowly missed. Post-election Nazi-communist violence was substantially higher in towns represented by elected Nazi MPs, while no discontinuity appears before the election. Mechanism evidence from perpetrator coding, stormtrooper mood reports, and membership records suggests that representation without power redirected frustration toward the movement's violent wing. The findings show that electoral representation can intensify anti-democratic violence when far right parties win mandates but remain excluded from power.

articles_hidden.title: Что такое жертва? Концептуализация виктимизации в опросах
articles_hidden.authors: Ruslan Kuchakov; Dmitriy Serebrennikov
articles_hidden.abstract: В статье рассматриваются основные подходы к концептуализации и операционализации понятия жертвы в виктимизационных опросах. На основе обзора более чем полувековой исследовательской традиции выделяются нормативный и конструктивистский подходы к определению жертвы и анализируются их следствия для дизайна опросных инструментов. Во второй части работы реконструируются три традиции операционализации виктимизации на материале пяти опросов: NCVS, CSEW, SES, ICVS и Всероссийского опроса жертв преступлений (RCVS). Авторы предлагают рассматривать эти исследования через матрицу двух измерений: фиксация факта (или стилизованного факта) виктимизации и фиксация самооценки респондента в качестве жертвы. Показано, что выбор стратегии измерения предполагает поиск баланса между юридической строгостью, обеспечивающей сопоставимость с официальной статистикой, и конструктной валидностью — способностью улавливать реальный опыт виктимизации, в том числе не распознанный самим респондентом. Другой компромисс — уже ресурсный — образует своего рода невозможную триаду: при ограниченном бюджете и времени интервью нельзя одновременно максимизировать содержательную широту опросника, лонгитюдную глубину и статистическую точность (надёжность) оценок. При этом сама лонгитюдная глубина достигается по-разному — от повторных кросс-секционных срезов, где каждая волна опрашивает новую выборку из той же совокупности, до панельных дизайнов, отслеживающих одних и тех же респондентов. Именно последние — панели с наблюдением за одними и теми же людьми — из-за бюджетных ограничений по сей день остаются редкостью.

articles_hidden.title: The chilean health model in the context of latin america. 40 years of economic crises, spending policies and reforms
articles_hidden.authors: Camilo Cid Pedraza; Mauricio Matus-Lopez
articles_hidden.abstract: This chapter analyzes the relationship between economic crises and health reforms in Latin America, with an in-depth focus on the Chilean case, from the origins of its health model to the present day, including a reflection on its possible future developments. The Chilean health model, as it is known today, was designed amid the international crises of 1975 and 1982 and the political crisis of the dictatorship, and it was consolidated during the economic growth of the 1990s. Its most significant reform, developed following the Asian crisis of 1997, resulted in the AUGE Plan, adopted in 2005, which increased access to a defined set of health conditions without changing the model's underlying structure. The 2008 global financial crisis, and later the 2019 social crisis, opened a new stage of debate over structural change, in which the segmentation between the public insurer (FONASA) and the private insurers (ISAPRES) has come to be seen as the central obstacle to an equitable and solidarity-based health system. The regional analysis shows that this relationship between crises and reforms is not unique to Chile, but follows a broader Latin American pattern, moving from market-oriented reforms in the 1980s and 1990s toward a growing consensus, strengthened by the COVID-19 pandemic, in favor of universal, solidarity-based public health systems.

articles_hidden.title: Are geographical and socioeconomic contexts exchangeable? On simple means versus random effects in the study of health inequalities
articles_hidden.authors: Juan Merlo; Kani Khalaf
articles_hidden.abstract: Multilevel random-effects (RE) models are standard in social and geographical epidemiology. They rest on the assumption of exchangeability, which means that, before seeing the data, we have no reason to distinguish one group from another: group means become draws from one common distribution. RE models were developed for repeated measurements within individuals where a shared physiology underwrites the assumption, and partial pooling improves prediction. A silent transfer later applied the same machinery to schools, hospitals, neighbourhoods and, recently, to intersectional strata. There exchangeability fails twice: individuals are not repeated measurements of their group, and groups are social positions produced by directional forces such as racism, not draws from a common distribution. We review strict, conditional and tolerant readings of exchangeability and show that they agree: social and intersectional categories are not exchangeable, as this would paradoxically require the absence of the unjustified inequalities which are the very object of study. In many intersectional analyses, shrinkage erases the small and deviating strata, where inequality lives. Modelling injustice as dispersion around a mean domesticates rather than denounces it. For describing realised health inequalities we recommend Simple-Means MAIHDA (S-MAIHDA). Here, each stratum is estimated from its own individuals, and uncertainty is reported openly rather than smoothed. RE models keep their legitimate uses, such as prediction, cluster-randomised trials and the propensity models of causal S-MAIHDA. Exchangeability is not a property of the software. It is a claim about the world, to be justified in every application.

articles_hidden.title: A Minimal Axiomatic Definition of Democratic Procedure: Count-Based Aggregation with Autonomy and Non-Coercion
articles_hidden.authors: Giulio Vidotto
articles_hidden.abstract:
This paper proposes a minimal axiomatic characterization of democratic procedures by combining structural requirements with conditions concerning individual freedom. Rather than starting from substantive conceptions of democracy, the paper treats a decision procedure as a function from profiles of individual expressions to collective outcomes, and asks under which minimal conditions such a procedure may still be called democratic. Four conditions are taken to be jointly required: universal expression, count-dependence, autonomy of judgement, and absence of coercion.
The main distinction introduced by the model concerns two failures that are often treated together, although they occur at different levels: coercion in expression, where individuals cannot state what they judge, and lack of autonomy in judgement formation, where the judgement itself has been shaped by manipulation or systematic distortion. Once these two loci are separated, a procedure may satisfy universal participation and count-based aggregation, and nevertheless remain democratically defective because what is counted is either not freely expressed, or not autonomously formed.
Methodologically, the paper adapts a measurement-theoretic distinction, that between latent and observed variables, to normative procedural theory. The resulting account remains institutionally neutral: it does not presuppose elections, representation, deliberation, or any specific institutional form, but provides a formal language for analyzing collective choice mechanisms, including referenda, digital voting systems, and algorithmic forms of governance.

articles_hidden.title: One meal, not the next: a two-day RCT testing effects of increased plant-based availability on direct and later food choice
articles_hidden.authors: Lotte Patricia de Lint; Wilhelmina Elisabeth Adriana Metje van Rookhuijzen; Rachelle de Vries; Emely de Vet
articles_hidden.abstract: Replacing animal-sourced foods with plant-based alternatives benefits the environment, animal welfare, and public health. Nudges have been found to promote plant-based selection in the moment, but whether they influence later, non-targeted behaviors remains underexplored. Effects on non-targeted behavior could make interventions more effective if they promote consistency in later plant-based choice, or less effective if they trigger compensatory animal-based choice. In a two-day randomized controlled trial (n = 200), we evaluated a Nudge plus intervention delivered on day 1. The intervention combined an increased availability of plant-based to meat sandwich varieties (3:1 vs. 1:3) with a post-choice identity cue informing plant-based choosers that their choice signaled they care about the environment. We assessed intervention effects on targeted behavior (day-1 plant-based lunch choice) and non-targeted behavior (day-2 plant-based lunch choice and 24-hour animal product consumption). Furthermore, we tested whether such effects were mediated by environmental self-identity or moderated by plant-based eating motivation. The increased availability tripled targeted plant-based choice, from 22% in the Reference condition to 66% in the Intervention condition. We detected no main effects of the intervention on either non-targeted outcome, with equivalence tests indicating a negligible effect on 24-hour animal product consumption. There was no evidence of mediation via environmental self-identity or moderation by plant-based eating motivation. Increasing plant-based availability produced a large immediate positive effect on plant-based choice, while the Nudge plus produced no detectable compensatory shifts in non-targeted behavior. These findings support increasing the relative availability of appealing plant-based over meat-based options in food service settings.

articles_hidden.title: Peace or Push? Understanding Global Patterns of Refugee Return
articles_hidden.authors: Mae MacDonald
articles_hidden.abstract: Return is the main way refugee crises end, yet there have been few cross-national studies of when it actually occurs. A central expectation of the refugee regime is that refugees remain abroad while home is unsafe and return as security improves. Yet using a novel global dataset, I show that most returns occur during ongoing conflict, while many refugees remain abroad long after wars end. To explain these patterns, I argue that asylum countries and international organizations play major and underrecognized roles in shaping return, largely overlooked by existing micro-level research focused on refugees’ concerns about security at home. Return is substantially higher when refugees face exclusion policies or conflict in asylum countries, and when donor-funded UNHCR assistance lowers the costs of return. I introduce the Global Refugee Return Dataset, covering 293 origin--asylum dyads from 1980 to 2023, which documents returns systematically undercounted by UNHCR and provides new global data on de facto refugee conditions and UNHCR financing.

articles_hidden.title: Quais os impactos da Lei  de Acesso à Informação  (LAI)?
articles_hidden.authors: Jorge Lucas; Ana Paula Lima dos Santos; João Pedro Cavalcanti Silva
articles_hidden.abstract:
O estudo busca avaliar os impactos da implementação da Lei de Acesso à 
Informação (LAI) sobre a transparência pública, a accountability e o controle social no 
Brasil, com base em uma revisão sistemática de 32 trabalhos. Os resultados indicam 
efeitos principalmente institucionais e organizacionais: a LAI contribuiu para 
institucionalizar o direito de acesso à informação, expandir os mecanismos de 
transparência ativa e passiva, criar condições para o controle social e modificar 
práticas internas de gestão da informação. Contudo, os efeitos são heterogêneos e 
predominantemente qualitativos. Embora diversos órgãos tenham criado portais, 
Serviços de Informação ao Cidadão (SICs) e regulamentações locais, a simples 
disponibilização de informações não garante transparência efetiva, accountability ou 
redução de irregularidades. O único estudo quantitativo identificado não encontrou 
associação estatisticamente significativa entre as medidas de transparência e a 
redução da corrupção ou da má gestão nos municípios analisados.

articles_hidden.title: The Kia-Hyundai vehicle theft surge: the roles of anti-theft devices and co-occurring offenses
articles_hidden.authors: Graham Farrell; John Roman
articles_hidden.abstract: Between 2019 and 2023, vehicle theft in the United States increased 40 percent. This study addresses this as a natural experiment, using a quasi-experimental design for causal inference to attribute the increase to theft of Kia and Hyundai vehicles manufactured without engine immobilizers. It is conservatively estimated that by the end of 2024 there were over 1.1 million excess vehicle thefts and over three hundred thousand excess co-occurring offenses including homicides, violence and other serious offenses. The evidence indicates that the withdrawal of situational crime prevention measures can increase crime and criminality and that the long-term national crime declines cannot be taken for granted. Additional implications are identified.

articles_hidden.title: How Parties Reshaped Class Participation: The Central Role of Parental Abstention
articles_hidden.authors: Giacomo Melli
articles_hidden.abstract: Labour’s programmatic realignment in the 1990s withdrew a generation of working-class adults from electoral politics. Abstention rose disproportionately in the working class, reshaping the formative environments of subsequent cohorts. This paper traces the lagged intergenerational effects of that shift on class inequalities in turnout. The analysis draws on linked parent-child data from the British Household Panel Survey and Understanding Society (1992-2025), in which parental class position and electoral participation are observed directly during respondents’ formative years, and combines random-effects panel models with parametric and nonparametric decomposition. The association between class origin and adult turnout is stable across cohorts socialised before and after realignment. What differs is the distribution of formative environments: exposure to parental abstention is substantially more unequal across class origins in the later cohort. Parental participation accounts for over forty per cent of the post-realignment class-origin gap, net of class destination and educational attainment, and counterfactual estimates suggest that equalising exposure would return the gap to pre-realignment levels. Class inequalities in turnout are therefore in part the lagged consequence of party strategy, transmitted through households and carried into the electorate by successive cohorts.

articles_hidden.title: How should VAWG be measured in the new UK strategy to halve it in ten years?
articles_hidden.authors: Sylvia Walby; Brian Francis
articles_hidden.abstract:
New metrics to evaluate the UK government’s strategy to halve violence against women and girls in
ten years are proposed. If the strategy to reduce violence against women and girls is to concern the
whole of government and the whole of society, then its measurement needs to mainstreamed not
confined to a separate silo. Three issues in building metrics are identified and resolved: strategic
(mainstreaming rather than a separate silo), conceptual (defining ‘women and girls’ and extending
violence to include non-domestic; distinguishing between different forms of ‘violence’); and
technical (strengths and weaknesses of different data sources and statistical techniques). While the
new government headline metric of a combined measure using a single data source has problems.
Modifying the combined metric and adding five supporting metrics and two additional data sources
would address these, achieving compatibility with the main statistical series on violent crime,
making visible the scale of the gender gap in more serious forms of violence, such as homicide, rape,
and high frequency victims, and making visible specific forms particularly relevant to Black,
minoritised and migrant women. This contribution to the indicators in the UK Strategy engages
global debates while focusing on the English context with its specific epistemic systems that engage
policy and data.

articles_hidden.title: Geographic Diversity and the Strategic Placement of Immigrant Candidates
articles_hidden.authors: Verena Fetscher; Ilayda Yücel
articles_hidden.abstract: Immigrant-background populations remain underrepresented in national legislatures. A common explanation is that parties perceive immigrant-background candidates as electorally costly and therefore place them disproportionately in unwinnable contests. Existing research, however, pays little attention to the geographic concentration of immigrant-background populations, which can create electoral incentives as well as risks. We argue that parties strategically nominate immigrant-background candidates where demographic diversity generates electoral opportunity. Using original data on all candidates in German federal elections from 2002 to 2025, we show that immigrant-background candidates are more likely to be nominated in districts with larger immigrant populations, especially where those districts are electorally competitive. We further show that these nomination patterns can translate into electoral gains, but the effect is limited. The strongest evidence comes from Turkish co-ethnic dynamics, and the electoral benefits are concentrated in the Social Democratic Party, which has historically had the closest ties to Turkish-background voters in Germany.

articles_hidden.title: Converging Across Generations? Intergenerational Integration into Associational Life
articles_hidden.authors: Mia Stenbro Lorenzen; Anders Bastrup Jørgensen; Hans-Peter Y. Qvist
articles_hidden.abstract: This article examines the extent to which immigrant-native gaps in voluntary association involvement, a key dimension of associational life, narrow across generations. Neo-assimilation theory suggests broad intergenerational progression, whereas segmented assimilation theory points to more heterogeneous trajectories across groups with different civic and religious backgrounds. To test these expectations, we examine intergenerational differences in voluntary association membership, active participation, and volunteering among non-Western immigrant-origin adults aged 18-50, using linked survey and register data from the Danish Citizenship Survey (N = 4,273). Logistic regression analyses reveal substantial intergenerational progression toward native levels of involvement. While first-generation immigrants are markedly less involved than natives, childhood immigrants and second-generation immigrants display involvement levels substantially closer to, and in some cases indistinguishable from, those of natives. Progression occurs broadly across groups with different civic and religious backgrounds, and groups with more distant backgrounds do not consistently exhibit less progression. KHB decomposition analyses further reveal that socioeconomic attainment and, especially, citizenship status account for substantial shares of the observed intergenerational progression, ranging from 40-47% for membership to 80-86% for volunteering. Overall, the findings extend neo-assimilation theory’s expectation of broad intergenerational progression to associational life and highlight the importance of structural and formal incorporation in this process.

articles_hidden.title: Effects of Questionnaire Notifications on Engagement and Attrition in an Ecological Momentary Assessment Study: Longitudinal Observational Study
articles_hidden.authors: Daniel Dvořák; Martin Kreidl; Martin Tancoš
articles_hidden.abstract:
Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) studies are widely used in mobile health (mHealth) research and interventions. EMA requires participants to repeatedly open short questionnaires announced by smartphone notifications, so notification scheduling is a central design decision. Yet evidence on how repeated prompts shape short-term engagement and long-term attrition remains fragmented.

We examined (a) how notification order within a measurement window relates to the timing and likelihood of questionnaire opening, and (b) whether the number of notifications within a burst relates to permanent disengagement, in a 12-month, multi-burst smartphone EMA study of Czech adolescents.

We analyzed paradata from the FUTURE project, an observational EMA study of 201 adolescents (13–17 years). Four 14-day bursts each contained up to four short questionnaires per day, with up to 10 notifications per questionnaire window. Time from first notification to opening was modeled with Cox survival models with respondent-level frailty. Permanent dropout was modeled with logistic regression at the person-burst level. We tested whether demographics, timing, and the momentary phone context (screen activity, app use) moderated the notification effects. Analyses used Stata 18.

A total of 26,007 questionnaires were notified. Of these, 17,668  (67.9%) were opened. Within a measurement window, among questionnaires still unopened, later reminders were associated with a slightly higher chance of opening (hazard ratio [HR] 1.13, 95% CI 1.06–1.19; P<.001), and this estimate was stable across all models, and we found no sign of within-window reminder fatigue. Gender, age, and socioeconomic status changed this pattern only marginally. The phone context mattered more. When the screen was already on (interaction HR 0.862, 95% CI 0.846–0.878), or social media (HR 0.884, 95% CI 0.856–0.913) or messaging (HR 0.884, 95% CI 0.844–0.926) was in use (all P<.001), reminders were less efficient. Regarding study dropout, 86 of 201 participants (43%) disengaged permanently. More reminders within a burst were associated with slightly lower odds of study dropout (fully adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.981, 95% CI 0.965–0.996; P=.01), a small association that was stable across all model specifications (OR 0.978–0.984).

In this adolescent EMA study, engagement was front-loaded: most openings came soon after the first prompt, but even later notifications had a positive effect on questionnaire engagement. So, within each measurement window, more prompts are better. This holds across all socio-demographics. Repeated reminders showed no sign of backfiring on study dropout. In fact, more reminders went with slightly lower study dropout. Responsiveness depended on what the phone was doing just before the first prompt. Context-aware prompting (avoiding prompts especially if a social media or a messaging app are open) is a more efficient design lever than simply adding reminders.

articles_hidden.title: Is a Fourth Contingency Necessary in Social Theory? A Constructive Critique
articles_hidden.authors: Georgi Sarov
articles_hidden.abstract: Contingency is a paradigm that opposes determinism, yet itself proves limited in its ability to explain the macro level. This article analyzes the epistemological foundation of both contingency and deterministic grand theories and establishes that both reduce objective reality in a manner that renders them possible, yet contradictory. A heuristic approach to reduction is proposed, deriving a solution to overcome it through a deductively argued necessity for a fourth contingency – one that manifests only in free and open deliberation concerning the true, the beautiful, the meaningful, and the useful. The fourth contingency is necessary where social change is carried out, but it is ignored in the reproduction of social models, where contingent rearrangements concern the redistribution of tensions and of the price. The latter is an inadequate solution: it does not remove social tensions but raises the production cost of social life.

articles_hidden.title: Questionnaire Design and Rater Cognition in 360-Degree Performance Appraisal
articles_hidden.authors: Saber Mirzaei Ahandani; Simin Ebrahimi Lialekol
articles_hidden.abstract:
Questionnaire design may play an important yet underexamined role in shaping the quality of performance appraisal data. This study examines whether redesigning response formats in a 360-degree feedback system is associated with improvements in rating behavior, response quality, and psychometric consistency. Drawing on cognitive processing and response-process perspectives, we compare a traditional numeric Likert-format questionnaire with a redesigned format incorporating behaviorally descriptive response options, modified visual presentation, and variable response ordering.
Data were collected across two appraisal periods within a large production organization employing more than 25,000 individuals. A total of 26,672 questionnaires were distributed, and 18,621 responses were obtained for the evaluation of approximately 900 managers in different levels. Following the redesign, participation rates increased from 47% to 79%, and internal consistency reliability improved from Cronbach’s α = 0.902 to α = 0.939. Response distributions also became less concentrated in extreme categories and more evenly distributed across intermediate categories, indicating greater rating differentiation and reduced response bias.
These findings are consistent with the argument that behaviorally descriptive response formats encourage greater cognitive engagement and reduce reliance on heuristic responding during performance evaluation. The study contributes to performance appraisal and multisource feedback research by highlighting the role of questionnaire design in shaping response processes, rating behavior, and measurement quality. Together, the findings provide evidence compatible with the view that relatively small and scalable questionnaire design modifications may enhance cognitive engagement, improve measurement quality, and increase the validity and practical usefulness of organizational appraisal data.

articles_hidden.title: A Reader’s Guide to the Rubin Report
articles_hidden.authors: John Levi Martin
articles_hidden.abstract: This was written for those readers of the Rubin report who are outsiders to the discipline of sociology, and look to this report as a guide to the state of this field.  Given the publicity this report has received, it would be reasonable for them to imagine that there is warrant for its claims.  There have been many responses to this report, but (as far as I know) none that have simply focused on whether she actually marshaled evidence to support her arguments, and whether she correctly represents her sources.

articles_hidden.title: Heterogeneous Effects of Local Government Financing Channels on Industrial Structure: Evidence from Provincial-Level Panel Data in China
articles_hidden.authors: Liangkun Shi; Huanqi Wu; Hanfei Yang
articles_hidden.abstract: Local government financing channels provide an essential perspective for understanding the investment decisions of local governments and their economic effects. In China, broadly defined local government debt includes two categories: statutory debt and the debt incurred by local government financial vehicles (LGFVs). This paper uses provincial-level panel data from 2016 to 2025, constructs a data-driven industrial structure index, and estimates a two-way fixed-effects model controlling for the overall debt scale. The empirical evidence suggests that the different financial channels on industrial structure are associated with different and opposing changes in industrial structure. When the debt composition shifts toward LGFV debts, the share of relatively high-productivity efficiency industries increases, particularly that of the tertiary sector. In contrast, when the debt composition shifts toward statutory debt, the share of relatively low-production efficiency industries increases, particularly that of the secondary sector. Therefore, the composition of local government debt, rather than its scale alone, is relevant to changes in regional industrial structure.

articles_hidden.title: V-FIRST: A Formal Syntax for Intelligence Requirements Construction (Vance Formula for Intelligence Requirements Syntax and Testing)
articles_hidden.authors: Marnie Vance
articles_hidden.abstract: Writing a priority intelligence requirement appears simple. Getting it right is not. One poorly built sentence at the start of the intelligence process can waste collection and leave decision-makers without usable answers. Doctrine defines requirements and places them in planning processes yet offers no method for constructing them. A review of public sources finds no published syntactic standard. V-FIRST v1.0 fills that gap. Named for its place at the start of both the intelligence process (Planning and Direction) and the collection management process, it sets fixed sentence forms for each level, component formulas, provenance keys, and a verb taxonomy tied to standards of proof. It answers a need first noted in a 1960 Studies in Intelligence call for “an adequate theory of requirements.” Released openly, V-FIRST is available for instruction, testing, adoption, and refinement.

articles_hidden.title: "Fill Out this Survey": Capabilities and Detection of Agentic Browsers
articles_hidden.authors: Renata Topinkova; Carsten Schwemmer
articles_hidden.abstract: Researchers increasingly rely on people to produce data through online interfaces. Agentic browsers create a new challenge for these workflows because they can navigate websites and complete tasks on a user’s behalf with little technical knowledge or effort. We evaluate whether three consumer-facing agentic browsers can complete online surveys and whether recently proposed measures can detect or prevent their use. The agents received only one simple instruction, "Fill out this survey", without detailed prompting or technical optimization. We tested technical screening measures, visible and invisible CAPTCHAs, AI-specific prompt-injection checks, consistency across a longer survey, and the completion of several surveys from a single instruction. The agents completed surveys with little or no user input, maintained assigned demographic profiles, and passed all tested prompt-leaking and jailbreak-style checks. Browser metadata did not reveal automated participation, and invisible reCAPTCHA was consistently passed by some browsers. Visible reCAPTCHA created the strongest barrier, although agents could sometimes solve it or return control to the user. These findings show that widely available AI agents can take over tasks intended for human participants while producing responses that appear coherent and plausible. This raises broader questions about how researchers can verify that supposedly human-generated data were actually produced by humans.

articles_hidden.title: Self-Employment in Mothers’ Careers After First Birth: A Comparison of South Korea and the United States
articles_hidden.authors: Wonjeong Jeong
articles_hidden.abstract: Motherhood can reorganize women’s paid work across wage employment, self-employment, and nonemployment. Yet research on mothers’ employment trajectories has rarely examined self-employment as a distinct arrangement. This paper asks where self-employment appears in mothers’ careers after first birth and how its position differs between South Korea and the United States. Using the Korean Labor and Income Panel Study and the Panel Study of Income Dynamics, I follow first-time mothers from the year of first birth through ten years afterward. Descriptive and sequence analyses show that roughly one in five mothers experiences self-employment at least once, although neither country has a continuous self-employment trajectory. In Korea, self-employment more often follows nonemployment and is primarily full-time, appearing within trajectories that lead back into paid work. In the United States, mothers more often enter self-employment from wage work, and part-time self-employment also appears briefly within wage-centered trajectories. These differences show that the same employment status can occupy different positions in mothers’ careers. Self-employment is likely to become increasingly important within workers’ careers as gig and platform work expand and artificial intelligence reshapes occupations and industries. Future research should examine how these changes alter pathways into self-employment and how labor protections, social insurance, and family-support policies can account for its distinctive risks and rewards.

articles_hidden.title: Is 'Realism' the Best Way to Explain International Relations?
articles_hidden.authors: Aarav Ghosh
articles_hidden.abstract: Evaluating whether realism constitutes the premier theoretical framework for explaining international relations requires strict adherence to clear epistemological benchmarks: explanatory range, parsimony, and Lakatosian progressiveness. This essay argues that structural realism remains the superior general theory of global politics. By anchoring its explanatory architecture within a stable, parsimonious core defined strictly by systemic anarchy and the distribution of capabilities, realism accounts for the widest variety of macro-phenomena (including polarity, balancing dynamics, and security dilemmas) without sacrificing its structural utility. While prominent rival frameworks such as liberalism, neoliberal institutionalism, and constructivism provide descriptive richness for localised interactions, they systematically trade breadth for depth by introducing redundant causal variables. Through a sophisticated Lakatosian methodology, this paper demonstrates how realism utilizes its positive heuristic to absorb empirical anomalies into a protective belt of auxiliary hypotheses, successfully preserving its core structural baseline while generating independently verified theoretical progress.

articles_hidden.title: Wasted Bonus? The Urgent Case of Rebuilding the Education-Labor Alignment in Indonesia
articles_hidden.authors: Muhammad Daffa Adjisena
articles_hidden.abstract: Indonesia's demographic bonus is usually described as peaking around 2030 and closing in 2045. Projections from the 2020 Population Census indicate the opposite: the age structure was most favourable in 2020, and has worsened in every projected year since, crossing 50 dependents per 100 working-age people in the early 2040s. Its composition is changing too: by 2050, nearly half of dependents will be people over 65, not children who later enter the workforce. The cohorts that decide the outcome are already in school. This scoping review maps what is known about the fit between Indonesia's education system and its labour market from 2013 to 2025, and locates where the evidence stops. Reported under PRISMA-ScR, searches covered OpenAlex, Crossref, ERIC, DOAJ, Garuda and SINTA alongside government sources in English and Indonesian. Of 762 records screened, 259 were included, charted to a common template and synthesised thematically. Co-occurrence of curriculum and labour-market concepts was mapped across a 640-record bibliographic corpus. Of the 259 included studies, 169 appeared from 2023 onward. Reported graduate deficits are consistently interpersonal, adaptive and digital rather than technical, with employers, students and researchers converging independently. Unmet employer demand concentrates in green, blue, digital and entrepreneurial work, the areas where training and measurement are weakest. More than 70% of vocational teachers in practical subjects lack the digital competence their curriculum assumes. Curriculum and labour concepts co-occur at 0.56 times the rate chance predicts, while each literature is internally dense at 1.58 and 2.61; Kurikulum Merdeka appears alongside employability, unemployment, skill mismatch or work readiness in no study. The two literatures do not run in parallel; they avoid one another. Indonesia is changing what it teaches faster than it measures what those changes do to employment, with less time to correct course than standard accounts of the demographic bonus imply.

articles_hidden.title: Dignity Defense Model : A Study on the Structural Mismatch in Employment of Female University Students in China and Its Shaping Mechanism on the Decline in Fertility Rate
articles_hidden.authors: Di Yuan; ZY Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: Millions of female university graduates in China face a severe shortage of standardized office jobs with weekends off each year. This structural mismatch exacerbates employment pressure. Drawing on empirical data from the Anhui provincial civil service examination, this paper proposes a “dignity-defense-oriented reproductive decision-making model.” Confronted with the gap between high career expectations and labor-market reality, female university students, motivated by dignity defense and risk aversion toward the motherhood penalty, prefer survival strategies such as “slow employment” and the “civil service examination craze” over marriage and childbearing. These choices significantly suppress the overall birth rate. To address this dilemma, the paper recommends reconstructing the university employment-quality evaluation system and disciplinary structure, introducing national policies that reduce the motherhood penalty, and promoting a shift in the macro-market toward consumption infrastructure centered on independent women.

articles_hidden.title: You cannot decompose injustice: interaction, intersection, random effects and simple means in the evolution of MAIHDA
articles_hidden.authors: Juan Merlo
articles_hidden.abstract: Random effects intersectional analysis has promoted the multidimensional study of health inequalities, and the intersectional application of Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA) is increasingly used to describe them. Its usual implementation fits an empty random effects model followed by a model adjusting for the variables that define the strata, and reads the remaining between-stratum variance as the intersectional effect. In this essay I trace how that convention grew, including my own contribution to it, and explain why my opinion has changed. Intersectionality, as originally formulated, is not about statistical interaction. The expression "more than the sum of its parts" refers to the uniqueness of a social position, not to an arithmetic operation. Intersectional strata are indivisible analytical units. I propose the term intact strata for strata kept whole in the analysis. I recall that random effects shrinkage describes a modelled population rather than the observed one, and present Simple-Means MAIHDA (S-MAIHDA) as the canonical design for the framework. Each stratum is estimated from its own individuals, and the three MAIHDA components, specific contextual effects (SCE), general contextual effects (GCE) and discriminatory accuracy (DA), are obtained on the probability scale. Keeping strata intact does not banish interaction. It relocates it, as effect modification between the intact stratum and the structural axes, such as geography, time or institution, along which the position is lived. You cannot decompose injustice. You can describe it whole, and you can measure what the structures around it do to it.

articles_hidden.title: Modelación Lógico-Proposicional y Reducción Forense Frente a la Infoxicación Procesal: Epistemología Jurídica "Desde Abajo" en la Defensa del Parque La Valvanera  /  Logical-Propositional Modeling and Forensic Reduction Against Procedural Information Overload: "Bottom-Up" Legal Epistemology in the Defense of La Valvanera Park
articles_hidden.authors: Luis Felipe Narvaez Galindez
articles_hidden.abstract:
RESUMEN:
El presente artículo analiza las asimetrías epistémicas y procesales en el litigio de derechos colectivos en Colombia. Desde la sociología reflexiva de Alvin Gouldner y la Investigación-Acción Participativa (IAP) de Orlando Fals Borda, se examina la resistencia comunitaria frente a la privatización del Parque La Valvanera en Pitalito, Huila. Se documenta la trayectoria del colectivo popular desde la tutela hasta el cauce contencioso-administrativo, abordando el ensayo decolonial con Enrique Dussel y categorías autónomas. Frente al dilema de Audre Lorde sobre las herramientas hegemónicas, se fundamenta cómo el repliegue provisional de los conceptos propios y la adopción de la lógica formal constituyeron una apropiación táctica de la racionalidad procesal dominante para salvaguardar un derecho material inminente, preservando la doctrina comunitaria para el debate sociológico formal. Asimismo, ante la infoxicación procesal desplegada por las demandadas mediante el aporte desarticulado de 800 MB de expedientes, se formaliza la introducción de un modelo algebraico booleano (V = A ∧ B ∧ C). Se expone la operacionalización de tres silogismos deónticos, una matriz de confesión cruzada y la extensión del modelo a defensas herméticas mediante prueba documental de puro derecho, situando la argumentación técnica como compuerta procesal hacia la Sentencia Anticipada (Art. 182A del CPACA).

ABSTRACT:
This article analyzes the epistemic and procedural asymmetries in public interest litigation in Colombia. Drawing upon Alvin Gouldner's reflexive sociology and Orlando Fals Borda's Participatory Action Research (PAR), it examines community resistance against the privatization of La Valvanera Park in Pitalito, Huila. The paper documents the collective's trajectory from an initial injunction (tutela) to administrative proceedings, addressing decolonial theory grounded in Enrique Dussel and bottom-up categories. Engaging with Audre Lorde's dilemma regarding hegemonic tools, it theorizes how setting aside indigenous concepts in favor of formal logic was a tactical appropriation of dominant procedural rationality to safeguard an urgent collective right, preserving autonomous doctrine for scholarly debate. Confronted with procedural information overload deployed by the defendants through the disorganized submission of 800 MB of files, the paper formalizes the introduction of a Boolean algebraic reduction model (V = A ∧ B ∧ C). It details three deontic syllogisms, a cross-party admission matrix, and the model's extension to airtight defenses via documentary evidence of pure law, positioning technical argumentation as the procedural mechanism for an Early Judgment under Article 182A of the CPACA.

articles_hidden.title: LLM measurements that agree with human coders overall can still distort specific effects
articles_hidden.authors: Alexander K. Moore; Bingqing Li; Shane Wang; Matt Thomson
articles_hidden.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adopted in the social sciences as surrogates for human coders. Standard practice validates them by their correspondence with human measurements of the same stimuli using statistics like correlation. However, overall correspondence can conceal biases that distort specific claims. We demonstrate this with open-weight LLM ratings of 568 food and 1,811 scene photographs. Ratings inflate, attenuate, or reverse effects, and improving overall correspondence with prompts can improve one contrast while worsening another. Rankings also elevate some categories and demote others beyond what random errors of the same size typically produce. Across six prompts, some of these errors are shared, so sampling across prompts may continue to mask biases. We propose validating LLM coders against specific claims they will test rather than the general coding task.

articles_hidden.title: Research on Gender Contradictions in Contemporary China: Structural Pressures, the Negativity of Marital Surplus, and the Gender Projection of Class Contradictions
articles_hidden.authors: Yuan Di; ZY Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: Against the backdrop of a sustained decline in marriage and birth rates in China and intensifying gender tensions, traditional explanations centered on individual preferences or gender norms are insufficient to account for the structural mechanisms involved. Drawing on the economics of marriage and the family, this paper examines how rising costs of housing, weddings, bride price, childbearing, and education affect men's decisions to enter marriage, as well as how the expansion of higher education, the shortage of standardized professional employment, and the motherhood penalty shape women's opportunity costs associated with marriage. Building on these factors, together with declining expectations of economic growth, changing lifestyle expectations, and the rising utility of singlehood as an alternative, the paper proposes the “Dual Marriage Costs–Expectation Mismatch Integrated Model” (the Di Formula) and uses “marital surplus” to characterize the comprehensive net benefits of marriage relative to singlehood. The paper argues that contemporary gender relations in China involve more than a conflict of values, but separately rising direct marriage costs for men and opportunity costs for women, together with a widening structural mismatch between modernity-based expectations and real resource constraints. When marital surplus declines and eventually becomes negative, individually rational decisions to postpone or forgo marriage may, in aggregate, contribute to declining marriage and birth rates and intensified gender tensions. Marriage is therefore increasingly shifting from a traditional mechanism of family cooperation toward a high-cost, high-risk, long-term economic decision.

articles_hidden.title: Identifying a Conflict’s Cause: The Theme-Enablers Framework
articles_hidden.authors: Moorthy Muthuswamy
articles_hidden.abstract:
Conflict studies lack a replicable method for establishing causation because existing frameworks 
conflate an ideology-driven conflict's cause with dependent variables it produces. This bottom
up shortcoming necessitates a top-down approach beginning with a causal framework. The 
Theme-Enablers Framework identifies a conflict's animating theme, its institutional enablers, and 
the agendas they propagate as separable, measurable variables, enabling simultaneous internal 
and external causal validation from the same dataset. The framework is reproducible, falsifiable, 
and generalizable to ideology-driven conflicts for which comparable societal-level data on 
themes, enablers, and agendas can be assembled. This article introduces a methodological 
package combining the framework with difference-in-differences estimation and regression 
analysis to identify and validate causal structure. The methodology is tested on the Islamist 
movement across five world regions and 20 lands, then applied to out-of-sample data from 
Britain, America, India, Gaza, Afghanistan, and Iran. The results demonstrate how the 
framework identifies a conflict's root cause and distinguishes it from downstream effects. The 
designs converge on a much-overlooked cause with direct policy implications: religious leaders 
leverage the Sharia platform to radicalize communities and obtain political power.

articles_hidden.title: Tracking nature dependencies and nature-related risks: integrated environmental-economic accounting in Australia
articles_hidden.authors: Crystal Bradley; Sarah Taylor; Michael Vardon; Mitchell Lyons; Sarah Clement; Carl Obst
articles_hidden.abstract: Ecosystems and the services they provide underpin economic production and human wellbeing, yet these dependencies are poorly measured and rarely monitored. As a result, conventional economic statistics often fail to show how ecosystem decline may threaten production and wellbeing. The missing information can be supplied by the United Nations System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA), an international statistical standard for tracking environmental stocks and flows, including ecosystems and their services, which is interoperable with the System of National Accounts (SNA). We assess how a linked system of SEEA and SNA accounts can be used to measure and track nature-economy dependencies, including the transmission of physical risk. We argue that accounting for ecosystem services provides the main connection between nature and the economy. The connection depends upon accounts using consistent classifications and typologies, which we call material join keys, so that information about ecosystems, ecosystem services, industries and economic activities can be reliably linked. Applying the approach to Australia, a gap analysis shows that existing ecosystem service accounts already track several of the dependencies most important and at risk from ecosystem decline, but only partially, and that priority new accounts for water and food security, health, climate resilience and supply chain resilience are needed to close the remaining gaps. Realising the potential of integrated accounting supports the mainstreaming of natural capital considerations into decision-making and public policy, and the proactive management of nature-related risks.

articles_hidden.title: Food Environment Policy Index for the German States: A structured policy analysis with expert consultations
articles_hidden.authors: Franziska Wiebke; Peter von Philipsborn; Anette E. Buyken
articles_hidden.abstract:
Abstract
Introduction
Subnational governments can play an important role in influencing food environments, particularly in multilevel governance systems such as Germany, where multiple levels can introduce policy and legislation. Yet the extent to which subnational governments, including the German States, use this potential remains largely unexplored. To make the scope of subnational food environment policies explicit, comparable and assessable, we developed a state-specific Food Environment Policy Index (Food-EPI), using Germany as an example. 
Methods
The INFORMAS Food-EPI served as the starting point for our analysis. To adapt it to the subnational level, we followed an iterative process drawing on four data sources: i) legal and policy documents and secondary sources; ii) key informant interviews; iii) written feedback from experts; and iv) an online expert workshop. 
Results
The state-specific Food-EPI covers 25 indicators across 12 domains, outlining the substantial scope of subnational governments to influence food environments. The policy domains are food labelling, advertising and marketing, subsidies, provision, retail and food service and waste, combined with six infrastructure support domains. We drew on 128 documents to identify 57 good practice examples from subnational governments and adapted the INFORMAS protocol into a streamlined four-step approach.
Conclusion
We demonstrate that it is feasible to develop a tool to assess food environment policy at the subnational level, that systematically outlines the substantial influence of subnational governments on food environments. Applying the state-specific Food-EPI in practice to German States is an important next step to further corroborate its practical relevance.

articles_hidden.title: Beyond the Dark Figure: A Causal and Probabilistic Analysis of Crimes Against Women in India
articles_hidden.authors: Rudrani Ghosh
articles_hidden.abstract: Most research on violence against women in India depends on administrative police records. However, this raw data often suffers from severe reporting biases and fails to account for massive population differences between districts. To address these flaws, this study applies causal inference, hierarchical modeling, and machine learning to better understand local crime dynamics. By combining two decades of National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) statistics with 2011 Census demographics, we map both the spatial distribution and the true sociological drivers of this violence. We found no evidence of geographic clustering; a Moran's I analysis shows the violence is distributed randomly across the country. Furthermore, our mixed-effects hierarchical models indicate that broad state-level policies explain less than 1% of the variance in local crime rates. Furthermore, by applying Pearl's do-calculus and Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), we isolate the causal effects of the male-female literacy gap and urbanization, proving that urbanization is the dominant driver of reporting rates. A Bayesian Structural Time Series (BSTS) correctly isolates the passage of the 2013 Criminal Law (Amendment) Act as an administrative reporting shock yielding an 88,879 annual case surge rather than a behavioral epidemic. Finally, Bayesian Belief Networks are utilized to model highly nonlinear sociological interactions, providing a mathematical framework for proactive risk assessment.

articles_hidden.title: The Economic Costs of Nepal's Open Border with India: A Case Study on Smuggling
articles_hidden.authors: Nirmal Gurung
articles_hidden.abstract:
The border between Nepal and India, which was opened in 1950 by the Treaty of Peace and Friendship, has created unprecedented conditions for developing cultural and social ties between the countries. However, the open border has also led to severe negative consequences for the national economy of Nepal. This research aims to discuss the effects of smuggling through the 1,880 km border and analyse the situation in the context of the foreign trade deficit and the deteriorating economic situation in the country.
Based on the data presented by the study, it is possible to draw the conclusion that smuggling contributes significantly to the trade deficit between Nepal and India. Smuggling of gold, drugs, agricultural products, and people constitutes a substantial part of trade between the countries. It is reported that 42.5% of the officially recorded trade between Nepal and India is smuggling, which results in a loss of 33.5 billion rupees for the Nepalese economy. In addition to the loss from unofficial trade, the state loses 3.58 billion rupees in duty and 3.71 billion rupees in value-added tax. The article also reports that the trade deficit in Nepal this year amounts to NPR 180 billion, of which a considerable part is caused by smuggling.
Thus, the current situation in which Nepal allows free trade between the countries is extremely disadvantageous for the national economy. The study provides multiple examples that prove the severity of the problem, including the cases of Badhaiyatal and Bardibas, where the largest seizures of marijuana, gold, and peas in recent years were registered. According to official data, 30,000 people are trafficked illegally into Nepal every year, resulting in significant losses for the economy. The causes of the problem include the initial policy of open borders, insufficient control mechanisms, corruption, and taxation issues. However, the authors of the article believe that a smart border is necessary to ensure the prosperity of the Nepalese economy through trade with India.
